new: Same as MSPDI Task/Resume: on a suspended task, the planned restart of the remaining work.
Same as MSPDI Task/ResumeValid. On a task with actualStart and no actualFinish, false means suspended with no resume date, and GRS does not use a date in resume.

Same as MSPDI Task/PercentComplete, except that GRS recalculates the value as actual working time (actualStart to actualFinish, or to stop) over planned working time (start to finish), times 100, rounded, with no cap at 100. With no planned working time, as on a milestone, the value is 100 once actualFinish is present, else 0.
note: rounded kept as an adjective participle

new: Calendar days over which GRS fades the start of the Plan Bar, to show that the start is not firm. Rectangle: the start edge slants. Chevron: sets the start notch depth. note: the bar -> "the Plan Bar": the fade lies inside start..finish (doc-shape-map why); "notch", "tip" are plain words, not glossary parts

new: As fadeInCalendarDays, for the finish (on a chevron, the tip depth). GRS writes the value to MSPDI as a Task/ExtendedAttribute.

new: A task group: one row of the Task Group Panel and one row in the Task Group Area. Task groups form their own tree, separate from the WBS (Task.parentTaskUid), and GRS does not write task groups to MSPDI.
The id of the task group.
The parent task group. Absent means a top-level task group (depth 1).
The task that this task group represents in the WBS. Absent means the task group represents no task. This property does not decide the name of the task group.
The order of this task group among the task groups under the same parent.
The task group name. Absent means an unnamed task group; GRS shows an empty title. GRS never copies a task name into this property after the task group exists.

Whether the task group is open, closed or hidden in the Task Group Panel. auto follows documentSettings.taskGroupAutoExpandDepth; temporarilyExpanded stays open until the next Zoom to Fit or vertical zoom out, and then becomes auto.
note: Zoom to Fit kept: the spec names the command so (docs/spec/_source/display-words.json)

new: The name of the group that may edit this task group. When present, GRS refuses edits to the tasks in this task group. Absent means anyone may edit.
The color of the row of the task group in the Task Group Area. Absent means GRS draws no color; {"kind":"theme"} draws the theme color.
note: longer than before (band -> row of the task group in the Task Group Area)

new: Lowest height of the row of the task group, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100; absent means no lowest height. verticalZoomRatio does not change this height.
The URL the task group links to. Absent means no link.
The title of the task group link. Absent means no title.
Which task group GRS draws a task in; every task is in exactly one task group. GRS stacks the tasks of a task group itself, in the direction that documentSettings.stackDirection gives.
The task; each task is in exactly one entry.
The task group that GRS draws the task in.
How GRS draws a task: the shape, the colors and the outline width of the task. Every task has exactly one TaskVisual.
The task that GRS draws with this TaskVisual; each task has exactly one TaskVisual.
Shape of a task that is not a milestone. Present exactly when Task.milestone is not true; a milestone holds milestoneShape instead.
Glyph of a milestone. Present exactly when Task.milestone is true.

The fill color of the Plan Bar. Absent means GRS draws no fill; fill and stroke may not both be absent. A custom color may give only one of light and dark: GRS works out the other when GRS loads the file.
Outline color of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar. Absent means GRS draws no outline.
Outline width of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar of the task, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. GRS writes 1 for a new task.
Where an imported task came from, so that importing the same file again updates the task instead of adding a copy.
The imported task in this document.
Project/UID of the file that GRS imported this task from. Absent when that file had none.
The UID of the task in the file that GRS imported the task from.
The id of the import that brought the task in; every import makes a new one. This id stands in for sourceProjectId when the file had no Project/UID.
The project.lastImportNumber of the last import that found this task in the imported file.
One task of an earlier plan, which GRS matches to the current task by uid and draws only as an outline over the current task.

The planned finish in the earlier plan.
Whether the task was a milestone in the earlier plan, so that GRS draws the task as a milestone.

One comment box. The tip of the comment box stands at a free point (an instant, a task group and a height within the row of the task group in the Task Group Area) or at one of eight points of the task or highlight box that the comment box snapped to.
note: longer than before (rule 1 and band -> row); "tip" is a plain word, not a glossary part

new: The id of the comment box.
